app_documentation:
The Flower Delivery App is a comprehensive e-commerce platform designed to streamline the process of browsing, purchasing, and delivering fresh flowers to customers. The application serves as a digital marketplace connecting flower enthusiasts with a curated catalog of floral arrangements, enabling seamless transactions from product discovery through final delivery. Built with modern web technologies including React for the frontend and Node.js/Express for the backend, the platform leverages PostgreSQL for robust data management and integrates with Stripe for secure payment processing and SendGrid for automated customer communications.

The app's main features include an intuitive flower catalog browsing system with category filtering and detailed product views, a dynamic shopping cart that allows customers to manage their selections before checkout, and a comprehensive order placement workflow that captures delivery details and payment information. Post-purchase, customers can track their orders in real-time through a visual status timeline showing progression from order placement through delivery. The platform also includes user profile management for saving addresses and payment methods, as well as an administrative interface for inventory management and order fulfillment operations.

The primary users of the Flower Delivery App are customers seeking convenient flower purchasing and delivery services, administrators who manage the flower inventory and oversee order fulfillment, and delivery drivers who handle the logistics of getting orders to their destinations. The mobile-first design ensures accessibility across iOS and Android devices, with responsive layouts that adapt to various screen sizes while maintaining WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. The application emphasizes visual appeal with high-quality product imagery, clear navigation patterns, and a nature-inspired color palette that creates a welcoming and trustworthy shopping experience.

Key technical capabilities include real-time inventory tracking to prevent overselling, secure payment processing through Stripe integration, automated email and SMS notifications for order updates, and a role-based access control system that differentiates between customer, admin, and delivery driver permissions. The platform's architecture supports scalability with indexed database queries, efficient cart management, and optimized API endpoints designed to handle concurrent user sessions and high-traffic scenarios during peak ordering periods.

glossary.Order Status: The current state of a customer order in the fulfillment pipeline, with possible values including Pending (order received but not yet processed), Processing (order being prepared), Out for Delivery (assigned to driver and in transit), Delivered (successfully completed), and Cancelled (order terminated before completion)
glossary.Payment Status: The current state of payment processing for an order, with possible values including Pending (payment not yet processed), Completed (payment successfully captured), Failed (payment attempt unsuccessful), and Refunded (payment returned to customer)
glossary.Delivery Time Slot: A predefined window of time during which a customer can request their flower delivery, typically categorized as morning (8am-12pm), afternoon (12pm-5pm), or evening (5pm-8pm) to accommodate customer scheduling preferences
glossary.Stock Quantity: The current available inventory count for a specific flower product, automatically decremented when orders are placed and updated by administrators through the inventory management interface to reflect real-time availability
glossary.Cart Item: A temporary record of a flower product that a customer has selected for potential purchase but has not yet checked out, stored in the cart table with quantity and timestamp information until either converted to an order or removed by the user
glossary.Baseline Artifact: A versioned snapshot of project documentation, design specifications, or technical schemas that serves as a reference point for tracking changes, managing revisions, and ensuring consistency across development cycles and support operations
